newsitem.title: UK: Safety group criticises Eurotunnel over fire.
newsitem.headline: Safety group criticises Eurotunnel over fire.

text.p: The Anglo-French Channel Tunnel Safety Authority said on Tuesday that last year's fire in the tunnel "exposed fundamental weaknesses" in operator Eurotunnel's "management of safety, which the company must recognise and correct at the highest level".

The authority's report makes 36 recommendations for improvement in safety policies, but does not go so far as to recommend a change to the basic design of Eurotunnel's heavy goods vehicles (HGV) wagons.
The Channel Tunnel Safety Authority said its report did
not "constitute authorisation for Eurotunnel to restart HGV services" and said it would advise the Anglo-French Intergovernmental Commission separately about the operator's proposals for a restart.
The authority said it needed to be satisfied that Eurotunnel could rectify the faults before commercial service could resume "at its former level".

"A thorough analysis ... raises important questions about the overall safety of the system in these and similar circumstances, and has brought to light faults and weaknesses which must be corrected," it said in a summary of the report.

"Before commercial service may be resumed at its former level, all of these questions must be answered by Eurotunnel to the satisfaction of the Channel Tunnel Safety Authority. Eurotunnel must, in particular, convince the Safety Authority that it is possible to ensure the safe evacuation of passengers in all circumstances," the authority added.
Eurotunnel shut down its freight services after last November's blaze, which swept through a main tunnel creating tens of millions of pounds of damage.

The Kent Fire Brigade, which helped fight the blaze and was involved in the CTSA inquiry, had criticised the design of Eurotunnel's freight wagons, claiming that it created a blow-torch effect once the fire was underway.
But the CTSA's report stopped short of calling for a re-design of the open-sided wagons.

"The report makes no recommendation regarding change to the basic design of the existing HGV rolling stock, although a number of recommendations are made affecting the on-board systems and testing of the locomotives and amenity coaches," the authority said.
Eurotunnel's own internal inquiry had cleared its equipment of any fault but admitted to "avoidable delays" in tackling the fire.
Eurotunnel's shares firmed 0.5 pence to 70.5 by 0945 GMT in London.
